references.text: Here the distribution of peoples according to their languages is mentioned, providing context that the whole earth originally had one language (Gen 11:1) before the Tower of Babel event.
Ham's descendants are distributed according to their languages, families, and nations—a situation explained by the confusion of languages at Babel.
Shem's descendants are distributed according to their languages, which directly contrasts with the fact that the whole earth had one language.
God's confusion of humanity's single language is described here as a consequence of their rebellion, explaining the transition from one common language to many.
On Pentecost, the language barriers from the Tower of Babel event were overcome by the Holy Spirit, as everyone heard the gospel in their own language—a thematic contrast to Gen 11:1.
The prophet Zephaniah promises that God will give the peoples pure lips so that all may call upon the name of the Lord—an eschatological restoration of the linguistic unity broken at Babel.
A clear theological contrast: Babel's judgment (language diversity) as a consequence of human pride, versus Paul's reminder of God's purpose in language diversity.
